Mr. Arun Kumar Singla, AAG Haryana.
 Nidhi Gupta, J.
Present appeal has been filed by the injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.61,000/- granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panipat (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') vide Award dated 15.4.2002 passed in MACT Case NO.7/1998 filed u/s 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

Ld. Tribunal on the appraisal of facts, pleadings and evidence on record held that the appellant had been injured in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 25.12.1997 due to rash and negligent driving of Bus bearing registration No.HR-05A-8079 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle'), being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and 3.
The Tribunal awarded compensation as above along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till realization.
Liability to pay the compensation was joint and several.

FAO 916/2003(O&M)
2023:PHHC:068351 Ld. counsel for the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation on the ground that prior to the accident the appellant was a daily wager in an Oil Refinery and in the accident in question the appellant has suffered 8% permanent disability.

It is submitted that due to this disability, the appellant is unable to do the job that he was previously employed in as, in the accident, he suffered fracture of his left hand and right leg and multiple injuries on left shoulder,
forehead and his collarbone broke.

It is submitted that accordingly, in view of these facts Sant Raj vs Harpal Singh And Ors on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99060738/
1 compensation granted to the appellant deserves to be enhanced.

sentences.text: Per contra it is submitted by the ld. counsel for the respondent State that compensation as granted by the ld.
Tribunal is just and fair in the facts and circumstances of the case and need not be interfered with.
No other argument has been raised.
Heard ld. counsel.
During pendency of this Appeal, respondent No. 1/driver of the offending vehicle had expired.
Vide order dated 22.10.2019 this Court had granted last opportunity to ld. counsel for the appellant to implead legal representatives of deceased respondent no.1.

It is stated by the ld. counsel for the appellant that he is unable to trace the legal representatives of deceased respondent no.1 and since liability was joint and several, therefore, service upon legal representatives of deceased respondent no.1 be dispensed with at this stage.
Ordered accordingly.

The compensation awarded by the ld. Tribunal is reproduced hereunder in tabulated form:-
FAO 916/2003(O&M) 2023:PHHC:068351 Sr.No. Head Amount (in rupees) 1 Medical bills 7,200/- 2 Loss of Income 3,000/-
3.

Pain and suffering 10,000/-
4.

Attendant charges 2,000/-
5.

Special diet 2,000/-
6.

Transportation 8,00/-
7.

Future treatment 20,000/-
8.

8% disability 16,000/-
9.
A perusal of the record of the case shows that PW3 Dr. V.K. Malhotra, Deputy C.M.O., General Hospital, Panipat in his cross-examination has stated that "the patient was examined.
He had malunited fracture of left hand and malunited fracture of left clavicle.
There will be slight difficulty with the claimant in doing the work".
Thus, as per the above testimony of PW3, the appellant will experience 'slight difficulty in doing the work'.

However, Ld. Counsel for the appellant has been unable to apprise this Court as to the nature of the work of the appellant; and what difficulty, if any, has been experienced by the appellant in Sant Raj vs Harpal Singh And Ors on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99060738/
2 doing his work; and if so, to what extent.

sentences.text: Nonetheless, it remains undisputed that as per Disability Certificate Ex. P3, the appellant has suffered 8% permanent disability.

Accordingly, in the facts and circumstances of the case, in my view, it will serve the ends of justice if the compensation of Rs.61,000/- granted to the appellant is enhanced by an amount of Rs.50,000/- .
Further, the accident in the present case is of the year 1997 and present appeal is of the year 2003.

Accordingly, respondents are directed to ensure that payment of Rs.50,000/- is released to the appellant within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order, failing which FAO 916/2003(O&M) 2023:PHHC:068351 the appellant shall be entitled to interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization, to be recovered by the respondent State from the officer/official found responsible for the delay.
Disposed of in above terms.
Application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
 11.05.2023.
(Nidhi Gupta  Joshi Judge
